$comment: The set of legal documents this build serves, and the only source of LegalDocument rows.
LegalDocumentCatalog reads this at startup, hashes each file's bytes into ContentHash and
upserts one row per (documentType, version). Adding a version means adding an entry here and
a file beside it - never editing a published file in place, which is exactly what ContentHash
Versions are ordered by effectiveAt, not by string comparison: the 'current' document of a
type is the one with the latest effectiveAt that is not in the future.
Versions are the document's own 'last updated' date. These are the real published documents,
sourced from the alpine-angular-landing repo (src/app/components/legal); the placeholders they
replaced were never deployed. Any change here must be mirrored in that repo, or venta.gg and
$pendingComment: 'documents' is what this build publishes. '$pendingDocuments' is what has been drafted and is
waiting on counsel; the catalog reads neither the key nor anything under it, so a draft sitting
here is inert - not hashed, not served, not consented to, and not able to become the current
document of its type.
The five 2026-08-14 entries are the monetization legal groundwork. Every one of them carries a
'LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED' banner in its first line and is a DRAFT, NOT OPERATIVE TEXT.
They are pending rather than published for a reason that is not squeamishness: removing the
banner changes the bytes, and this directory's rule is that changed bytes are a new file plus a
new entry. So the reviewed text will always be a NEW file dated the day it was approved, and a
'documents' entry pointing at a draft could therefore only ever publish text nobody signed off.
Identity.Tests asserts exactly that: no document the manifest declares may contain the banner.
To publish one: counsel produces <type>-<approval date>.md without the banner, with a matching
'Last updated' line (the version IS that date - LegalDocumentCatalogTests checks the two agree),
and its entry moves into 'documents' with a real effectiveAt. Mirror it to alpine-angular-landing
in the same change.
privacy-2026-08-14.md supersedes privacy-2026-08-05.md and adds section 6, the fraud-prevention
processing purpose for hashed phone, device and payment-instrument identifiers. Publishing it
puts every existing account into consent-required for Privacy, which is correct and intended but
is a user-visible event to schedule deliberately rather than to ship as a side effect.
PaidServices, Refunds, Downgrade and Credit are new document types. Identity.Domain's
LegalDocumentType enum has only Terms, Privacy and Cookies, so those four need an enum member
before they can be published at all; the column is character varying(32), so no migration is
involved. None of the four belongs in ConsentService.RequiredDocumentTypes - only Terms and
Privacy may put an account into a consent-required state, and these are recordable but never
required.
